title: HTTP Gateway
description: REST gateway, wait/events endpoints, metrics, auth, CORS, and generated client

blocks.text: Hound includes a built-in HTTP gateway that exposes the full surface over REST: emit (fire-and-forget, batch, and blocking wait), a live job-finished event stream (SSE), Prometheus metrics, and the management API. External services emit jobs without a direct Redis connection; browsers can talk to it directly with CORS enabled.

Emit a single job — body: { event, data?, options? }
Emit multiple jobs — body: [{ event, data?, options? }]
Emit and hold the connection until the job finishes

blocks.text: The shortest path is app.listen() — it wires the app's management API into the gateway automatically:
hound.listen() works too when you want to pass the management instance explicitly, and createGateway() gives full control over hostname, CORS, and body limits:
The HTTP equivalent of emitAndWait(): the connection is held open until the job reaches a terminal state. The response tells you how it ended:

curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/emit/wait \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer my-secret-token' \
  -d '{"event": "report.build", "data": {"id": 7}, "options": {"timeoutMs": 15000}}'
A 408 means the wait window expired — the job may still be queued or running. The server caps the wait at 120s regardless of the requested timeoutMs.
When the gateway runs in a different process than the workers, configure a Broker on both sides so job-finished events reach the gateway — see the Broker page.
Server-Sent Events stream of every job that reaches a terminal state. Each message is event: job.finished with a JSON payload { jobId, queue, status, error? }. Filter to one queue with ?queue=name.

curl -N http://localhost:4000/events?queue=payments \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer my-secret-token'
The stream sends a heartbeat comment every 15s to keep proxies from closing idle connections, and open streams are closed cleanly on server shutdown.
Standard Prometheus text exposition. Queue lengths and processing counts are live reads from storage; completed/failed are per-process counters since the instance started.

# TYPE hound_uptime_seconds gauge
hound_uptime_seconds 3600
# TYPE hound_queue_length gauge
hound_queue_length{queue="default"} 12
# TYPE hound_jobs_processing gauge
hound_jobs_processing{queue="default"} 3
# TYPE hound_jobs_completed_total counter
hound_jobs_completed_total{queue="default"} 4096
# TYPE hound_jobs_failed_total counter
hound_jobs_failed_total{queue="default"} 17
The same snapshot is available programmatically via await hound.metrics() — useful for custom dashboards without scraping.
Available when a HoundManagement instance is passed to the gateway (app.listen() does this for you):

rows: List jobs (query: queue, status, limit, offset)
Get a single job — 404 if missing

blocks.text: Paginate listings with limit and offset — applied after sorting (newest first) and filtering:
curl 'http://localhost:4000/management/jobs?queue=payments&status=failed&limit=20&offset=40'
Set the auth option to require a Bearer token on all gateway requests. The comparison is constant-time:
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Without auth, any service that can reach the gateway port can emit jobs and access management endpoints.

For browser clients, set cors on createGateway() — true allows any origin, a string allows that origin only. OPTIONS preflights are answered without auth (browsers do not send Authorization on preflight). Request bodies are capped at maxBodyBytes (default 1 MiB) and oversized requests get 413.
generateClient() writes a typed HoundClient that wraps the gateway with the same type safety as direct hound.emit() calls. It is fully portable — no Deno, Hound, or Redis dependency, just fetch:

The client also exposes the full management API: client.management.jobs.find({ limit: 20 }), .get(), .delete(), .pause(), .resume(), .promote(), .retry(), and client.management.queues.find(), .stats(), .pause(), .resume(), .reset(). Missing jobs come back as null (mapped from the gateway's 404).
